newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P assigns A-/A-2 ratings to Wellington Airport.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns A-/A-2 ratings to Wellington Airport.

text.p: Ratings agency Standard and Poor's said on Thursday it had assigned its A- long-term and A-2 short-term credit ratings to Wellington International Airport Limited (WIAL).
S&P said the ratings outlook was stable.
S&P said the ratings reflected WIAL's strong business position servicing New Zealand's capital city, and solid passenger growth prospects.

"These strengths are offset by the significant increase in debt required over the next few years to finance the extensive terminal development program and the consequent narrowing of interest cover ratios," S&P said.
WIAL operates the only airport servicing Wellington.
S&P said increases in debt to finance a major capital programme to update the old airport terminal will weaken WIAL's financial profile significantly over the next few years.
"However, the airport's strong business position should enable it to retain a strong ability to meet its principal and interest obligations over the long term," S&P said.
